answer: Each epoch an agent reputation is graded by a randomly rotated panel drawn from a large validator pool, so no sybil knows which peers judge its work. Collusion only pays if the attacker holds a supermajority of the panel, and since the reshuffle hits like a pulse each round, buying enough identities to guarantee that grows exponentially expensive. Fake identities plus bribes cost more than any reward, so honest work dominates. Reputation flows like water cutting a canyon, and the sonnet-like structured randomness of rotation keeps every agent accountable to strangers, not friends.
